fixtures.note: Copy the fixture to a scratch dir and run there, never in place: evals edit files, and the fixture is pinned by tests/skill_fixture.rs. See README.md.

evals.name: near-limit-survey
evals.prompt: Which files in this project are getting close to their size limit?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `linecop --baseline <PCT>` with a warning band (around 85) rather than counting lines itself. It reports src/parser.rs at 75 of 80 code lines (93%) and src/tables.rs over at 89 of 80. It does not call parser.rs over the limit: it has 97 raw lines, but `count_mode: code` counts code only. No files mutated.

assertions.text: Ran linecop with `--baseline` below 100 rather than measuring with `wc -l` or by reading files
Reported src/parser.rs as near the limit and src/tables.rs as over it
Did not call src/parser.rs over its limit (its raw line count exceeds 80, its code count does not)

evals.name: grow-near-limit-file
evals.prompt: Add a `parse_duration` function to the parser that turns values like `90s`, `5m` or `2h` into seconds, using the unit table in src/tables.rs. Include a unit test.
evals.expected_output: Before writing, agent checks headroom (`linecop --baseline` or the config plus a run) and sees src/parser.rs at 75 of 80 code lines. It puts parse_duration in a new module (for example src/duration.rs, re-exported from lib.rs) instead of growing parser.rs past its limit. It does not make room by deleting comments, joining lines or raising the Rust limit. Afterwards `linecop` reports no file beyond src/tables.rs.

assertions.text: Checked parser.rs's headroom with linecop before writing the new code, not only after
Placed parse_duration outside src/parser.rs, or split parser.rs, so no file it touched exceeds its limit
Did not delete comments, join lines or otherwise compress existing code to make room
Did not change the `Rust` limit in .linecop.yaml
A final `linecop` run reports no violation other than the pre-existing src/tables.rs
Left the pre-existing src/tables.rs violation alone: mentioned it, did not exclude or edit it unasked

evals.name: failing-gate-generated-file
evals.prompt: The file size check is failing on this repo. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs linecop, finds src/tables.rs over at 89 of 80, and sees from its header (and README.md) that it is generated by scripts/gen_tables.py. It adds a narrow override for that file, preferably `exclude: true`, with a YAML comment giving the reason. The glob must match the scanned path (`./src/tables.rs` or `**/tables.rs`; plain `src/tables.rs` does not match when scanning `.`), and a rerun exits 0. It does not hand-split the generated file or raise the language-wide limit.

assertions.text: Identified src/tables.rs as generated and left its contents alone
Added an override scoped to that file rather than raising the `Rust` limit
Put a comment in .linecop.yaml next to the override saying why
Verified with a rerun that linecop exits 0

evals.name: paths-for-piping
evals.prompt: Give me a command that prints every file at 90% or more of its size limit, one path per line, so I can pipe it into another tool.
evals.expected_output: Agent answers `linecop --baseline 90 --format paths` and shows it printing ./src/parser.rs and ./src/tables.rs. It does not build a grep, sed or awk pipeline over linecop's text output or over `wc -l`.

assertions.text: Did not parse linecop's text output or count lines with another tool
